sections.content:
9,225 people

were counted on the census as "telephonists" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Telephonists receive and direct callers in commercial, industrial and other establishments, and operate telephone (public) and office (private) switchboards to assist with making telephone calls, and to relay incoming, outgoing and internal calls.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "telephonists" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "telephonists", 12.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "telephonists" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "telephonists" included:

  • horticultural trades
  • receptionists
  • elementary administration occupations (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "telephonists" there were more women than men (70.8% compared with 29.2%).

This means "telephonists" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "customer service occupations".

Men made up 29.2% and women made up 70.8% of "telephonists"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "telephonists" included:

  • waiters and waitresses
  • local government administrative occupations
  • officers of non-governmental organisations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "telephonists" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "telephonists" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "telephonists", 17.5% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (53.6% compared with 46.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.3%) than self-employed (4.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Liverpool, this is in the same region of the North West.
